clips.caption:
On The Kevin Trudeau Show, Kevin Trudeau points out a connection most people never make: poor sleep and low testosterone.

When you don't reach deep sleep, your body makes less human growth hormone and less testosterone. Kevin Trudeau says that's one real reason America has the highest rate of men needing ED medication of any country on earth.

His point isn't about the pill. It's about the sleep that comes before it - the deep, uninterrupted kind most men never reach.

Before reaching for a prescription, how many nights this week did you actually sleep through the night?

clips.send: A friend sends this to someone who always sleeps with their phone on the pillow - a little anxiety, an easy fix to try tonight.
clips.caption:
On The Kevin Trudeau Show, Kevin Trudeau walks through what's quietly wrecking people's sleep: the phone next to the bed.

He says a phone that's merely silenced isn't enough - it's still searching for Wi-Fi, and that signal adds to everything already stirring in the room. His fix: shut it off completely, and keep it in another room if you can.

For the racing mind that won't shut off either, he points to a simple amino acid, L-theanine, taken earlier in the day or an hour before bed, to calm the brain down naturally.

Where does your phone sleep tonight - on the nightstand, or in another room?

clips.caption:
On The Kevin Trudeau Show, Kevin Trudeau says the sheets people sleep in every night are washed in water with fluoride and chlorine, then scented with a detergent and fabric softener most people never question.

He says that combination gets inhaled all night and absorbed through the skin, and it can work against good sleep. His fix: organic, dye-free sheets, a scent-free hypoallergenic soap, and skipping the fragranced softener and dryer sheets entirely.

A small swap, he says, but one most people never think to make.

When's the last time you actually read the label on your laundry soap?

clips.caption:
On The Kevin Trudeau Show, Kevin Trudeau says there's a two-hour window almost nobody protects: midnight to 2 a.m., the only hours the body naturally releases human growth hormone.

Miss that window night after night, he says, and the body recovers slower and ages faster. Hit it consistently - lights out by 10 to 10:30 - and he calls the result the real elixir of youth, made by your own body, not injected into it.

No supplement replaces that window. Only deep sleep during it does.

What time did you actually fall asleep last night?

clips.caption:
On The Kevin Trudeau Show, Kevin Trudeau gives a simple test for whether you're actually sleeping well: how long it takes you to fall asleep.

More than five minutes, he says, and you're probably not reaching deep sleep. He adds a few more signs - a messed-up bed in the morning, waking up to use the bathroom, tossing and turning - each one a sign the body never fully shut down.

Miss deep sleep often enough, he says, and it shows up everywhere: energy, weight, mood, hormones.

How many of these signs describe your last night's sleep?
